newsitem.title: UK: Millennium tower plans for London turned down.
newsitem.headline: Millennium tower plans for London turned down.

text.p: Plans to build a 1,265 feet (385 metres) skyscraper in London's financial heart were blocked on Wednesday after English Heritage, the government conservation body, opposed the scheme.
The decision effectively puts paid to the plans for the transparent Millennium Tower, which would have been the tallest building in Europe.
The project can only now proceed if the Secretary of State for the Environment, John Selwyn Gummer, intervenes.
Sir Jocelyn Stevens, chairman of English Heritage, said after a meeting of the body's commissioners:
"Millennium Tower represents such a quantum leap in terms of scale, height and bulk that it would overwhelm the quintessential character of the capital."
Stevens stressed however that the tower, designed by leading architect Norman Foster, was a "very good-looking building" but it was simply in the wrong place in the City of London.
"It would disfigure the skyline. We believe that London's importance lies in its mixture of historic and other medium and low structures.
"London doesn't need a macho building to establish a place for itself as a world financial centre," he said.
The tower, on the site of the Baltic Exchange, which was damaged by an Irish Republican Amry bomb, has already been attacked by the Royal Fine Art Commission as "simply out of scale".
